title: GRPO groups, normalization and KL estimators
outcome: Compute group-relative advantages, expose degeneracy and weighting choices, and identify the sampling law required by a KL estimator.

exercises.title: Shift all rewards
exercises.hint: Both the mean and every reward shift together.
exercises.answer: Relative normalization removes a common level; it does not preserve information about absolute task success.

exercises.title: Inspect a constant group
exercises.task: Compare all-zero and all-one reward groups.
exercises.expected: Both produce zero relative advantages under the declared rule.
exercises.answer: These groups represent different absolute outcomes despite the same lack of within-group ranking signal.

exercises.title: Change length weighting
exercises.task: Give advantages-1,+1 to responses of length 2,4.
exercises.answer: A token average weights longer responses more heavily and defines a different objective from equal-response weighting.

exercises.title: Check the sampling law
exercises.task: Average case B KL terms under the old uniform policy.
exercises.expected: The value differs from current-policy KL.
exercises.hint: The identity requires expectation under the numerator policy p.
exercises.answer: Importance correction can recover the value expectation with adequate support, but has variance costs and does not by itself prove a gradient estimator is correct.

exercises.title: Separate value from derivative
exercises.task: Evaluate the centered two-action surrogate at zero log odds.
exercises.expected: Its value is 0 while its derivative is 0.5.
exercises.hint: Each centered advantage multiplies a different probability derivative.
exercises.answer: A zero average advantage or initial objective value does not imply absence of a learning signal.

exercises.title: Declare algorithm variants
exercises.task: Change standard-deviation correction, epsilon or token reduction.
exercises.expected: Record the change as part of the training algorithm.
exercises.hint: These settings alter advantage or gradient weighting.
exercises.answer: A shared acronym is insufficient to establish that two implementations optimize the same objective.

sources: GRPO outcome supervision and KL expression
